basics.name: Zhengyang (Jason) Qi
basics.label: Founding Research Scientist, Listen Labs
basics.summary: Zhengyang (Jason) Qi is a Founding Research Scientist at Listen Labs. His recent research explores how people reason, make decisions, and form expectations about the future, and how mid-training and reinforcement learning can help language models simulate these processes. He focuses on scaling these simulations across diverse individuals and situations, and on building realistic human simulators for training and evaluating long-horizon agents. Previously, he worked at Snorkel AI and Scale AI. He holds an M.S. in Intelligent Information Systems from Carnegie Mellon University and undergraduate degrees from Georgia Tech and Emory University.

work.name: Listen Labs
highlights: Build longitudinal representations of human context that capture how people's experiences, preferences, and expectations evolve over time and shape their decisions.
Develop reinforcement learning methods for post-training language models to simulate human reasoning and decision-making across diverse individuals and situations.
Scale human simulation models to support realistic behavioral modeling and the training and evaluation of long-horizon agents.

work.name: Snorkel AI
work.position: Senior Research Scientist, Agent RL & Evaluation Research
highlights: Designed and ran task curation and verification pipelines for SWE-Bench Pro, Terminal-Bench 2.0, OSWorld 2.0, PostTrainBench, and EDA computer-use agent tasks, spanning synthetic environment generation, verifier-validity checks, and LLM-as-judge and rubric-based review; delivered agent-task datasets, frontier coding-agent preference evaluations, and clinical-agent rubrics.

Researched reward hacking, verifier validity, and rubric failure modes in agent environments and evaluation pipelines to improve data quality; built RIFT (ICLR 2026 workshop), a rubric failure-mode taxonomy and automated diagnostics for auditing evaluation and reward signals.

Single-handedly built the company's agentic RL training stack on verl and Kubernetes: asynchronous, fault-tolerant rollout workers, sandboxed terminal-environment execution, and multi-node training on 64 H200 GPUs with Ray, Megatron, and SGLang.

Trained long-horizon terminal agents with GRPO, improving Terminal-Bench 2.0 from 5.6% to 13.4% (Qwen3-32B) and from 36% to 41% (Qwen3.5-27B) through environment selection, reward attribution with partial-credit assignment, rejection sampling, and on-policy distillation.
Published on automated benchmark design and milestone-based evaluation for RL; advised research direction and environment/task design for OSWorld 2.0.

work.name: Scale AI
highlights: Led post-training of multimodal LLM judge and reward models with reasoning RL and RLHF (SFT, GRPO, and human preference supervision), curating 60k+ evaluation and 300k+ training examples across multilingual instruction following, multimodal reasoning, STEM, and coding; the production judge outperformed GPT-4o on human reward and preference alignment.

Built an agentic auto-evaluation system for scalable oversight of human--AI data-generation pipelines; deployed on 10+ production pipelines, cutting human labeling cost by up to 60% while preserving calibration and human-judgment quality.
Built automated quality-control agents for RLHF rubric pipelines (RAG, tool use, multi-agent debate), outperforming baseline agents across deployments.

work.name: Carnegie Mellon University, Language Technologies Institute
work.position: Graduate Research Assistant; advisor: Prof. Graham Neubig
highlights: Researched interactive evaluation, social intelligence, multimodal ML, and reinforcement learning for language agents; co-built the SOTOPIA interactive evaluation platform (ICLR 2024 Spotlight) and the SOTOPIA-π self-play and self-reinforcement training pipeline, leading to publications at ICLR, ACL, and EMNLP.

Built research systems and datasets for simulated social environments, rubric-based evaluation, self-play training, multimodal interaction modeling (MMoE), and long-horizon dialogue understanding (Avalon).
